observations.quote: CHAP. II. Where that True Physick is to be Found.
observations.note: The chapter is headed and numbered as the place where the True Physick is to be found.

observations.quote: EVery thing that God created Good is extreamly perfect and incorruptible, as the heaven
observations.note: What God created good is perfect and incorruptible; the heaven is the example.

observations.quote: whatsoever is in these sublunary inferiour things hath a twofold Nature
observations.note: Things in the sublunary inferiour world have a twofold Nature, spelt out next as perfect and imperfect.

observations.quote: a perfect and an imperfect, that is, a fift Essence and the dreggs may be separated one from the other by fire
observations.note: The twofold nature is glossed: the perfect is a fift Essence, the imperfect the dreggs.

observations.quote: may be separated one from the other by fire
observations.note: Step of work: fift Essence and dreggs are separated from each other by fire.

observations.quote: the true medicine (or Physick) is wrapt up in rindes, barks, matrixes, receptacles, husks, garment and cottages
observations.note: The true medicine is said to be wrapped up in coverings.

observations.quote: as Almonds and all kernells are covered with bark and rind
observations.note: The covering of the medicine is put as a likeness: kernel inside bark and rind.

observations.quote: the same must be seperated from the impure Elements by the artificiall Anotomy of Chymists before we can come at the pure Medicine
observations.note: Step of work: the medicine is separated from the impure Elements by the Chymists' artificiall Anotomy before the pure Medicine is reached.

observations.quote: For the bonds are loosed by art and industry, and the faculties of healing set at liberty.
observations.note: What the separation does: art and industry loose the bonds and set the healing faculties free.

observations.quote: Wheat doth norgrow without a place, nor can we have meale without bran, neither is hony without a sting.
observations.note: Margin likenesses of a good thing that comes joined with something else (meal with bran, honey with sting), beside the twofold-nature passage.

observations.quote: Such Secrets are regenerated without any complexion of qualities.
observations.note: Margin: these things are called Secrets and are said to be regenerated without complexion of qualities.

observations.quote: those three Families of Nature, the Vegetable, Animall, and Minerall
observations.what: three Families of Nature, the Vegetable, Animall, and Minerall
observations.note: Nature is set out as three Families, the sources of medicines.

observations.quote: there is contained that True and specifix Physick of materiall distempers
observations.note: The True and specifix Physick is contained in all three Families.

observations.quote: which as hath been said
observations.note: Points back to an earlier statement that the Physick does not lie in the four outward qualities.

observations.quote: as Theophrastus learnedly discourseth
observations.name: Theophrastus
observations.note: The denial that the Physick lies in the four outward qualities is given with Theophrastus named as discoursing of it.

observations.quote: it is a certaine specifix vertue concealed in the very Seeds, naturally proceeding without art
observations.note: The true Physick is a specifix vertue said to be concealed in the Seeds.

observations.quote: which the Creator, that great Workmaster of all things, in the beginning of all the Creation planted in every growing thing by vertue of that omnipotent Word
observations.note: The Creator planted this hidden vertue in every growing thing at the beginning, by the omnipotent Word.

observations.quote: The faculties and vertue therefore wherewith mixt bodies are indued (like the soule in mans body from the beginning of the Creation) is not from without
observations.note: The vertue of mixt bodies is inborn from the Creation, like the soul in man's body, not from without.

observations.quote: nor infused into them by a momomentaneous position of the Stars, nor made up of a fortuitous meeting of Atomes
observations.note: Two origins of the vertue are denied: a momentary position of the Stars, and a chance meeting of Atomes.

observations.quote: it proceedeth not from the body nor the mixture of the body or visible forme, for then it could not be separated without the destruction and corruption of the body and forme
observations.note: The vertue is not from the body or its mixture; the reason given is that it can be separated without destroying the body.

observations.quote: as we see in Cinamon and Pepper, whose virtues being extracted either by art, or vanishing by age and long keeping
observations.note: Example: the virtues of Cinamon and Pepper are extracted by art or vanish with keeping.

observations.quote: the mecanick sciences of the Three principles
observations.note: The Three principles are named as one set whose sciences have their vigour in spirits and tinctures; these lines do not say what they are.

observations.quote: the actions of Cures proceed from the Spirits and vitall Tinctures of the spirits, not from the bodies or dead Relloceous qualities
observations.note: Cures come from Spirits and vitall Tinctures, not from bodies or the dead qualities. The word stands here as Relloceous, in CH2.2 as Relollaceous.

observations.quote: Heaven is the framer of the externall edifices, not of the Secrets, Wonders and mysteries that dwell in them.
observations.note: Margin: Heaven frames only the outward buildings, not the Secrets that dwell in them.

observations.quote: have their force by subministration from the Heaven
observations.note: Here inferior things have their force from the Heaven; CH2.3 says their vertue is not from without nor infused by a position of the Stars, and N133 that Heaven frames only the outward edifices, not the Secrets.

observations.quote: it is granted by the Interpreters of Secret Nature
observations.name: Interpreters of Secret Nature
observations.note: The view that everything in the Universe is also in Man is given as granted by the Interpreters of Secret Nature.

observations.quote: there is nothing in the whole Universe, every particular whereof is not also in that Microcosm Man
observations.note: Man as Microcosm holds every particular of the Universe; given as granted by the Interpreters.

observations.quote: is not also in that Microcosm Man, as hath been said
observations.note: Points back to an earlier place where this was said.

observations.quote: the seeds of all things lye hid in him
observations.note: The seeds of all things, of Stars, Mineralls, Spirits and more, are said to lie hid in Man.

observations.quote: this Symmetricall concord and Physicall anagoge
observations.note: The likeness of Man and Universe is named as one thing: a Symmetricall concord and Physicall anagoge.

observations.quote: it hath been the part of True Physitians to enquire, that if the internall Heart of the Microcosm or Man should be sick, how they might borrow strengthning remedies from his Parent
observations.note: True Physitians seek remedies for man's sick inner Heart from his Parent, the outer Heart, the two being alike.

observations.quote: the externall Heart of the Microcosm which is one like the other
observations.note: The outer Heart is printed as that of the Microcosm, the same name as man's; CH2.7 calls the outer counterpart Macrocosmicall.

observations.quote: (if not in outward, yet in inward figure and forme)
observations.note: The likeness of the two Hearts is said to be inward, not outward.

observations.quote: which remedies are analogically represented
observations.note: The remedies are said to be represented by analogy, pointing to a correspondent sense.

observations.quote: those three shops of Cures
observations.note: The three sources of remedies are called three shops of Cures.

observations.quote: All the whole inferiour Nature is divided into three principall parts, i. e. Vegetable, Animall, and Minerall.
observations.what: three principall parts, i. e. Vegetable, Animall, and Minerall
observations.note: Margin names the three parts the three shops refer to.

observations.quote: For God created an inexhaustible supply of medicines, and distributed to every Country sufficient for it selfe.
observations.note: God made medicines without end and gave each Country enough for itself.

observations.quote: Gold (which cheareth up the Spirits when a man hath enough of it in his purse)
observations.note: Gold as medicine is set beside gold as money in a purse; the bracket gives a second, everyday sense of cheering the Spirits.

observations.quote: Antimony and the like, which are produced out of the Element of Water, as Gemms and precious stones in shells are generated of drops of water
observations.note: Minerals such as Antimony are said to come from the Element of Water, like stones in shells from drops of water.

observations.quote: which by a specifick and Harmonicall vertue serve to cure and comfort the heart
observations.note: These things cure and comfort the heart by a specifick and Harmonicall vertue.

observations.quote: which sage Antiquity hath without rashnesse or superstition attributed to them
observations.name: sage Antiquity
observations.note: Minerals bear Magicall and Hieroglyphicall Characters, attributed to them by sage Antiquity.

observations.quote: that doe sufficiently insinuate to Inlightned men, and Magically disclose their hidden vertue to those more secret Phylosophers that are instructed therein
observations.note: The Characters disclose the hidden vertue only to enlightened, instructed philosophers.

observations.quote: by Natures just decree, with-hold their benigne and vitall Element from those that possesse them
observations.note: The choicest things withhold their vitall Element from those who merely possess them.

observations.quote: As he that hath much Gold may know nothing of its medicinall vertue.
observations.note: Margin: the owner of much Gold may know nothing of its medicinal vertue.

observations.quote: many there are who confound the Universall Lawes of Nature, and yet thinks to partake of her Banquet in the end
observations.note: Many confound Nature's laws and still expect her Banquet.

observations.quote: the Gold would discover most Divine actions if it were rightly refined, and had its power reduced into act by a Naturall and due Resolution
observations.note: Step of work: Gold rightly refined has its power brought into act by a Naturall Resolution.

observations.quote: for there is but one way to Resolve and to compound things, because Art and Nature, like mother and daughter, consent to each other
observations.note: There is one way only to Resolve and compound, since Art and Nature agree like mother and daughter.

observations.quote: Art imitateth Nature and supplyeth its defects; it correcteth, chastiseth, assisteth and promoteth, yea it exceedeth Nature.
observations.note: Margin: Art imitates, mends and even exceeds Nature.

observations.quote: few men have this gift of God bestowed on them, so as to make solid and massy Gold potable, that it may be drunk
observations.note: Making Gold potable is a gift of God given to few.

observations.quote: Amongst Vegetables there is Saffron, Rue, Balme, Scordium, Celandine, Mace, Ocymum, with six hundred of the like.
observations.note: Vegetable medicines are listed under the vegetable family.

observations.quote: Amongst Animalls there is Hart's horn, Unicorns horn, the Bone in Staggs hearts
observations.note: Animal medicines are listed under the animal family.

observations.quote: All which being rightly prepared in due manner, doe cure the diseases of the Heart
observations.note: The listed things cure the Heart only when rightly prepared; the manner is not given in these lines.

observations.quote: not (as I have said) by their Externall superficiary qualities
observations.note: Points back to what the author has said before: cure is not by outward qualities.

observations.quote: but by an Internall, proper, specifick, harmonious, similer virtue
observations.note: They cure by an inner, specifick, similer virtue.

observations.quote: for all things whatsoever serve to our health, are all contained in the Spirits, which onely know how and where to find out the disease
observations.note: All that serves health is contained in the Spirits, which alone find the disease.

observations.quote: the earthy part is altogether dead, husks and rinds beget nothing, the Spirits onely in the bodies of things doe all
observations.note: The earthy part and husks are dead; only the Spirits in bodies act.

observations.quote: The Formes in thee medicines or Astra's of the medicaments separated by Alchymie from their bodies are the true Directoryes
observations.note: The Formes are glossed as Astra's; separated from their bodies by Alchymie, they direct the cure.

observations.quote: not the body, but the Astrum or hidden Heaven gives all the direction
observations.note: Astrum is glossed as hidden Heaven; it, not the body, directs.

observations.quote: every medicine striveth to get to its place, and seeketh after that member that is like unto it
observations.note: Each medicine seeks the bodily member like itself.

observations.quote: magnetick vertue which may well be called the inexpressible property
observations.note: The magnetick vertue by which like seeks like is named the inexpressible property; a letter of the word before it could not be read.

observations.quote: as the true Phylosophicall Phisitians have diligently observed by long Experience the most undouted Rule of all
observations.name: the true Phylosophicall Phisitians
observations.note: That like applies itself to like is given as observed by the true Phylosophicall Phisitians.

observations.quote: Celsus the Roman Physitian confesseth of all Arts
observations.name: Celsus
observations.note: Celsus is named as confessing something of all Arts; the sentence as given does not say plainly what.

observations.quote: where by many good old country women have gone beyond great learned Physitians
observations.note: Country women are said to have gone beyond learned Physitians; whether as Celsus' confession or the author's own the text does not show.

observations.quote: Experiment, as also judgement, without knowledge is but fallacious difficult and fortuitous, but with Science it is true and infallible.
observations.note: Margin: Experiment without knowledge is fallacious, with Science true.

observations.quote: Experiment, as also judgement, without knowledge is but fallacious difficult and fortuitous, but with Science it is true and infallible.
observations.note: Margin says experiment without knowledge is fallacious, beside the text praising country women who outdo learned physicians.

observations.quote: The same may be sayd of the other six principall members and parts of mans body
observations.what: the other six principall members and parts of mans body
observations.note: Six further principall members are announced beside the Heart.

observations.quote: The external Macrocosmicall Braine is the Oyle of Silver, Water of the Sophire Emerold, Mosse, Vitrioll
observations.note: The outer Braine of the great world is said to be these named things, which strengthen the inner Braine of man.

observations.quote: The flower or CHIBUR or Brimstone are a Balsam for the lungs and the whole breast.
observations.note: CHIBUR stands beside flower and Brimstone, as a Balsam for lungs and breast.

observations.quote: After this manner not only ordinary diseases are cured by every Dunce, but also those Chronicall, Astrall and fixed diseases
observations.note: In this way even chronic, Astrall and fixed diseases are curable.

observations.quote: the common sort of Physitians who know not the seat, seeds, nativities, roots, and centres of diseases judge to be incurable
observations.name: the common sort of Physitians
observations.voice: QUOTED: the common sort of Physitians
observations.note: Common Physitians, not knowing the seat and seeds of diseases, judge them incurable; the author reports this to reject it.

observations.quote: For there is no disease, as it is a disease, but there is a medicine for it
observations.note: Every disease has a medicine.

observations.quote: unlesse such as prodeth onely from the anger of the Divine Majesty by secret predestination, which cannot be found out by man
observations.note: The exception: disease from God's anger by secret predestination, which man cannot find out.

observations.quote: the cure whereof was never given to Physitians, but to the Apostles, who by true faith in Christ healed all Diseases
observations.note: The cure of such disease was given to the Apostles, not to Physitians.

observations.quote: unlesse with Pliny we should belye Nature in its perfections as an unjust Step-mother
observations.name: Pliny
observations.note: The view of Nature as an unjust Step-mother is given to Pliny and rejected.

observations.quote: whereas indeed she is the benigne Parent of all Things
observations.note: The author's own view against Pliny: Nature is the kind Parent of all things.

observations.quote: provident and wise Nature hath by naturall instinct bestowed upon poor bruite creatures the knowledge of their Remedies
observations.note: Nature gave beasts the knowledge of their remedies by instinct.

observations.quote: It were therefore great folly and sottishnesse to think that the great Creator would hide these things from men
observations.note: The author denies that the Creator would hide remedies from men.

observations.quote: the great Creator would hide these things from men
observations.note: Here hiding from men is denied; CH2.5 says the choicest things withhold their vitall Element and few have the gift of potable gold, and CH2.20 that the Word is not known to every one.

observations.quote: There is no cause to complaine of the want of medicines but onely of our ignorance of them.
observations.note: Margin: not medicines are wanting, only knowledge of them.

observations.quote: There are two sorts of Physitians, one cure miraculously, the other naturally by means.
observations.note: Margin divides Physitians into miraculous and natural.

observations.quote: there are two originalls of every disease, the one naturall, the other caelestiall
observations.note: Margin names two originalls of every disease.

observations.quote: the Caelestiall is cured by the Word of the Lord, the Naturall is recovered by naturall means
observations.note: Margin: each originall has its own cure.

observations.quote: Every Creature knoweth his proper remedy.
observations.note: Margin sums up the list of beasts and their remedies.

observations.quote: The Stork having eaten a Serpent, is cured with Organy.
observations.note: First of a list of beasts each cured by a named herb.

observations.quote: The Toad when stung or poysoned with any other venomous creature, eateth Rue, Sage or Plantin, or rubs the wounded part therewith and is recovered
observations.note: The Toad heals itself with herbs, by eating or rubbing.

observations.quote: therefore it is not good to eat Sage before it be washed
observations.note: A practical rule drawn from the Toad's use of Sage.

observations.quote: And other living creatures have found out other innumerable Hearbs.
observations.note: The list closes: other creatures have found countless other herbs.

observations.quote: would in this particular neglect his own children, which he created after his own Image, and prefer the Beasts before them
observations.note: No man in his wits will think the Father neglects his children, made after his Image, and prefers the Beasts.

observations.quote: how much rather will he subject the whole Creature, both things visible and invisible?
observations.note: From the gift of the Son the author argues that the whole Creature, visible and invisible, will be subjected to men.

observations.quote: The most High Author of Nature ath created Medicines out of the Earth
observations.note: God created medicines out of the Earth; margin N141 names Eccl. 38. beside these words.

observations.quote: Eccl. 38.
observations.name: Eccl.
observations.note: Margin names a writing beside the words on medicines created out of the Earth.

observations.quote: he hath commanded the Physitians to search them out and seasonably administer them to every distemper being by due faith prepared and made up
observations.note: The Medicines are created perfect; Physitians are commanded to search them out and give them, prepared by faith.

observations.quote: not defectives but perfect
observations.note: Here Medicines out of the Earth are perfect; CH2.1 says whatever is in sublunary things has a perfect and an imperfect nature.

observations.quote: all medicines which are appled to mans body become efficacious and obtaine their wholesome effect, not of it selfe, but by the gift of God
observations.note: Medicines work by the gift of God, not of themselves.

observations.quote: unlesse God be present and infuse virtue into the Hearbs what good can Dittany doe, or any other soveraigne medicine
observations.note: Without God present infusing virtue an herb does no good.

observations.quote: For unlesse God be present and infuse virtue into the Hearbs what good can Dittany doe
observations.note: Here God infuses virtue into herbs; CH2.3 says the virtue is not from without nor infused, and CH2.2 that it was planted in the beginning.

observations.quote: All these inferiour things, as living creatures, hearbs, stones, mettalls have their force by subministration from the Heaven, and the Heaven from the Intelligences, and these from the great Worker
observations.note: A chain of force: lower things from the Heaven, the Heaven from the Intelligences, these from the great Worker.

observations.quote: For the Elements live by the Firmament, the Firmament from the Intelligible World, and this onely in God, or his Eternall Word
observations.note: The same chain for life: Elements, Firmament, Intelligible World, God or his Word.

observations.quote: and the onely life of all, and in all, yet variously sprouting forth according to the subject into which it flows
observations.note: God is the one life in all, showing differently by the subject it flows into.

observations.quote: Will of the Lord is earnestly to be implored
observations.note: Margin: in natural things not Nature but the Will of the Lord is to be implored.

observations.quote: if we intend to doe any good with hearbs, we must not trust so much to them as to God
observations.note: Trust belongs to God more than to herbs.

observations.quote: Asa dyed because he trusted more to the Physitians then to God.
observations.name: 2 Chro.
observations.note: Asa is the example of one who died trusting physicians over God; margin N143 names 2 Chro. 16.12. beside it.

observations.quote: The Caelestiall Medicine onely, or the WORD of God
observations.note: The Caelestiall Medicine is said to be the WORD of God.

observations.quote: which is the Firmament of all Physick
observations.note: The Word is called the Firmament of all Physick, a use of Firmament other than the heaven of CH2.12.

observations.name: Psal.; Eccl.
observations.note: Margin names writings beside the passage on the Word as medicine.

observations.quote: in which lyeth hid, and from which proceedeth all force beyond any naturall actions
observations.note: All force is said to lie hid in the WORD; by it Medicines have power.

observations.quote: As the bark is not the kernell, so hearbs are not the medicines, but a signe onely of the Word signified.
observations.note: Herbs are said to be only a signe of the Word; the bark and kernel figure of CH2.1 now points to the Word.

observations.quote: Physick is two-fold in the Earth
observations.note: Physick is set out as two: Visible from the Father, Invisible from the Son.

observations.quote: ought not to be administred before there be a separation of the pure from the impure
observations.note: Visible Physick is to be given only after the pure is separated from the impure.

observations.quote: Invisible, from the Son by the Word, and is but one
observations.note: Invisible Physick is from the Son by the Word, and is one only.

observations.quote: the Hearb is not the medicine, for that is invisibly hid in God himselfe
observations.note: The medicine is said to be hid invisibly in God himself.

observations.quote: for that is invisibly hid in God himselfe
observations.note: Here the medicine is hid in God; CH2.1 has the true medicine in the kernel of things reached by the Chymists' separation, CH2.2 has the vertue concealed in the Seeds, and this paragraph itself speaks of the Hearbs in which the medicine is.

observations.quote: Almighty God could (and can) make men whole by the Prophets and True Cabalists with a word onely
observations.note: God heals through Prophets and True Cabalists with a word only; margin N145 names Acts 3.6. beside it.

observations.quote: Acts 3.6.
observations.name: Acts
observations.note: Margin names a writing beside healing by a word.

observations.quote: God is a living God, the NAME also of the living God is lively, and so the Letters of the living Name are also lively
observations.note: Life passes from God to his NAME and from the Name to its Letters.

observations.quote: True Magicians (by whom I doe not mean Nicromancers or them of the Black Art) those accurate searchers out of Nature
observations.note: The author says whom he means by True Magicians: searchers out of Nature, not Nicromancers.

observations.quote: framed at a certaine time according to the power of Heaven
observations.note: The Word written and the Characters or Signes are framed at a certain time by the power of Heaven.

observations.quote: far from all superstition, which ariseth onely from ignorance, without any prophanation or scandall of the Divine Majesty, or any wrong to Faith and Religion
observations.note: The author holds this work free of superstition and of wrong to religion.

observations.quote: otherwise it were better for us alwayes to be sick then to be cured with the dishonour of God
observations.note: Better always sick than cured with dishonour of God.

observations.quote: For Characters or constellated Names according to Agrippa, have no force from the Figureors Pronunciation
observations.name: Agrippa
observations.note: The view that Characters have force not from figure or pronunciation but from the Vertue or Office God or Nature ordained is given to Agrippa.

observations.quote: Such Names are the Divine Power.
observations.note: Margin says what such Names are.

observations.quote: There is no vertue or power either in Heaven or Earth which descendeth not from God
observations.note: All vertue descends from God and acts by his permission.

observations.quote: Medicines are visible bodies; Words are invisible bodies
observations.note: Medicines and Words are both called bodies, visible and invisible.

observations.quote: by the Spirit of God made One with Nature by his Word FIAT
observations.note: Herb or Word heals by the Spirit of God made one with Nature by the Word FIAT.

observations.quote: Concerning Characteristicalll Cure which affecteth Naturall operations by words pronounced, written, carved and hanged about the neck
observations.note: A kind of cure is named: by words spoken, written, carved, hung about the neck.

observations.quote: let him read Rog. Bacon of the wonderfull power of Art and Nature
observations.name: Rog. Bacon
observations.note: The reader is sent to Rog. Bacon for characteristical cure; no words of his are given.

observations.quote: Paracels. saith that Characters are
observations.name: Paracels.
observations.note: Margin gives Paracels. a saying on Characters; letters of it could not be read.

observations.quote: Physitians also have wrought great cures by the Created Word, or the incarnate Mercy
observations.note: Created Word is put beside incarnate Mercy; Physitians have cured by it.

observations.quote: all these things are done by the efficacy of the Triune and Divine Word onely, which healeth and preserveth all things
observations.note: All cures are done by the Divine Word only.

observations.quote: to whom the Pills and Syrups of all the Shops in the world could doe no good
observations.note: No remedy of the Shops could help those the Saviour healed.

observations.quote: Luke 11.14.
observations.name: Luke
observations.note: Margin names a writing beside the Saviour's miracle of the deafe and dumb.

observations.quote: he did it by One Word, and he is that Word, to wit, the increated Mercy of God
observations.note: The Saviour is said to be the Word, glossed as the increated Mercy of God; the same paragraph earlier says Created Word.

observations.quote: John 1.3. Not by bread alone, Mat. 4.4.
observations.name: John; Mat.
observations.note: Margin names writings beside the Word by which all things are made.

observations.quote: all that for certaine is wrought of God incarnate in his explicit and manifest bond of one Spirit filling all things inseperably gathered into one
observations.note: All vertue in creatures, in great and little world, is wrought by God incarnate in one Spirit that fills all.

observations.quote: which Spirit therefore is the only fulnes of the whole world
observations.note: This Spirit is the fulnes of the world and is given a name: The Fulnesse.

observations.name: Eccl.
observations.note: Margin names a writing beside The Fulnesse.

observations.quote: Nothing is made out of God, for in him all things live, are moved and doe subsist.
observations.note: Nothing is made outside God; all things live and subsist in him.

observations.quote: Grace exceedeth Nature, and the thing signified excelleth the signe.
observations.note: Margin: Grace above Nature, the thing signified above the signe.

observations.quote: This WORD of God, the First begotten of every Creature, is truly our Dayly Bread
observations.note: The WORD is said to be the Dayly Bread prayed for.

observations.quote: it is the supercaelestiall Mummy, the supernaturall Balsome comforting poor Mortalls more then Mans own Mummy or naturall Balsom
observations.note: The WORD is called supercaelestiall Mummy and supernaturall Balsome, set above man's own Mummy or naturall Balsom.

observations.quote: The vertue in bread is the blessing of God, yea God himselfe
observations.note: The vertue in bread is said to be God's blessing, God himself; the Word in food is the true Bread.

observations.quote: Man liveth not by bread alone, but by that which is in Bread
observations.note: Man lives by what is in bread, the Word; N149 gives 'Not by bread alone' with Mat. 4.4.

observations.quote: If the Word were not, or of it selfe were not the onely Bread, then the Earth would be our God
observations.note: Argument: were the Word not the only Bread, the Earth would be our God.

observations.quote: It is of mere mercy and goodnesse not of justice that we have both the bread of nourishment and of healing.
observations.note: Margin: bread of nourishment and of healing come of mercy, not justice.

observations.quote: Without this benediction the staffe of bread is broken, a God threatned his people by his Prophets.
observations.name: his Prophets
observations.note: Margin: without the blessing the staffe of bread is broken, given as God's threat through his Prophets.

observations.quote: This Word then is the true medicine that healeth all things, but is not known to every one
observations.note: The Word, the true medicine, is not known to every one.

observations.quote: nor can every Scholler treat and write of it though plunged over head and eares in the dusty learning of School-Divinity
observations.note: School learning does not fit a scholar to write of the Word as medicine.

observations.quote: our friend Theophrastus Paracelsus a Disciple of the Mosaicall and Living Phylosophy hath written of the Secrets of Nature and the Wonders of God
observations.name: Theophrastus Paracelsus
observations.note: Theophrastus Paracelsus is named as having written of the Secrets of Nature and the Wonders of God.

observations.quote: to wit, of the WORD of God INCARNATE which may be found in the Creatures
observations.note: The Secrets and Wonders are glossed as the WORD of God INCARNATE, to be found in the Creatures; margin N153 names writings beside it.

observations.name: John; Heb.; Psal.
observations.note: Margin names writings beside the incarnate Word.

observations.quote: by this Word, FIAT, the seed of the whole world, were Heaven and Earth created
observations.note: FIAT is called the seed of the whole world, by which Heaven and Earth were created and which works in all Creatures.

observations.quote: to which the Creatures are justly in subjection as to their own soule
observations.note: Creatures are subject to this Word as to their own soul.

observations.quote: that the MAGUS, the Wise man or Caelestiall Physitian performeth suddenly and much sooner by Characters and Stones with a most powerfull impression
observations.note: MAGUS is glossed as the Wise man or Caelestiall Physitian; he does at once by Characters and Stones what the Physitian does in time by HEARBS.

observations.quote: to wit, the Gamahaea of Influentiall Wedlock to the Terrestiall signe, by matrimoniall combination of the Superiors and Inferiors ASTRALLY
observations.note: The impression is glossed as the Gamahaea, a wedlock of heavenly influence to an earthly signe.

observations.quote: like a stretched cord, all the Superiour vertue floweth through every inferiour thing even to the utmost
observations.note: The tie of Nature is put as a likeness: higher virtue runs through all lower things like a stretched cord.

observations.quote: the inferiour passe through all to their Superiours, because the working Vertue is one
observations.note: Lower things also reach the higher, because the working Vertue is one.

observations.quote: Divine Matrimony
observations.note: The tie of higher and lower is named Divine Matrimony, a figure the paragraph repeats (Wedlock, matrimoniall, marriage).

observations.quote: many things may be done in Magick and Cabal by the intercession of the worlds marriage
observations.note: Much may be done in Magick and Cabal through the world's marriage.

observations.quote: in Hearbs Stones and Words there are great vertues.
observations.note: Margin calls the paragraph the explication of a common saying about Hearbs, Stones and Words.

observations.quote: And the True Cabalist (whom Paracelsus calls the Naturall Divine, who is equall to the Prophets
observations.name: Paracelsus
observations.note: The name Naturall Divine for the True Cabalist is given to Paracelsus.

observations.quote: whose mind being united and coaequant to God doth whatsoever he will, for he willeth onely what God doth
observations.note: The Cabalist's mind is united to God and wills only what God does.

observations.quote: he doth above Nature, DEALLY or like God accomplish complish in a moment by firme confidence and strong faith
observations.note: DEALLY is glossed as like God; the work is done above Nature, in a moment, by faith.

observations.quote: the very GATE of miracles in that Only Divine Name ISHUH in which all things are reckoned up and contained
observations.note: A single divine Name is set apart as the gate of miracles, containing all things.

observations.quote: that is he doth performe it in the WONDERFULL WORD by the Mind, Faith and Prayer, to wit, prayers made in Spirit and in Truth
observations.note: Doing it in the Name is glossed: in the WONDERFULL WORD, by Mind, Faith and Prayer.

observations.quote: The New Birth is the Field of Caelestiall Physick which healeth with a word without Externall means
observations.note: The New Birth is called the Field of Caelestiall Physick.

observations.quote: that one operation is in respect of God as the Artificer, and in respect of Man as the Instrument
observations.note: In this work God is the Artificer, Man the Instrument.

observations.quote: every creature is at the beck and command of their faith who are men innocent and taught in the Law of the Lord
observations.note: Every creature obeys the faith of innocent men taught in the Law of the Lord.

observations.quote: who are heard in all things whatsoever they pray for, witnesse Elias, Elisha
observations.name: Elias, Elisha
observations.voice: QUOTED: the books of the Kings; Wifd.
observations.note: Elias and Elisha are called as witnesses of faith that is heard; margin N156 names the books of the Kings and Wifd. beside it.

observations.quote: Read the books of the Kings. 1 Kings 3.12. Wifd. 7.
observations.name: the books of the Kings; Wifd.
observations.voice: QUOTED: the books of the Kings; Wifd.
observations.note: Margin sends the reader to writings beside the faithful who are heard.

observations.quote: Every Creature feareth and reverenceth his Name that made it.
observations.note: Margin: every creature reveres its maker's Name.

observations.quote: By prayer in Faith we obtaine all things, I mean (not a lazy, sluggish prayer, but) a constant asking, seeking, knocking
observations.note: Constant prayer in faith obtains all things.

observations.quote: I mean (not a lazy, sluggish prayer, but) a constant asking, seeking, knocking
observations.note: The author says what he means by prayer.

observations.quote: by faithfull Prayer we ascend in a straite and most sure way to the highest Wisdome of Divine and humane Things
observations.note: Faithful Prayer is the sure way to the highest Wisdome.

observations.quote: For in these Three principall Poynts also consisteth the whole Foundation of the Magicall and Cabalisticall Art
observations.note: Three points are set apart as the foundation of the magical and cabalistical art; that they are the Mind, Faith and Prayer named before is an interpretation, not stated.

observations.quote: as appeareth by Paracelsus in his third book of the Signature of Things
observations.name: Paracelsus
observations.note: The Three principall Poynts as foundation of the art are referred to a named book of Paracelsus.

observations.quote: Honour and Praise and Glory therefore belongeth to the Creator, who worketh all in all
observations.note: The praise for a cure belongs to the Creator.

observations.quote: the Physitian who is the obedient Minister of God and Nature
observations.note: The Physitian is called the obedient Minister of God and Nature.

observations.quote: there is no other reward due but that of his faithfull paines and Charity
observations.note: The Physitian is due only the reward of his pains and Charity.

observations.quote: For there is nothing at all of his own in it besides Art and right preparation
observations.note: Only Art and right preparation are the Physitian's own.

observations.quote: will not give his Honour to another
observations.note: God keeps his Honour to himself.

observations.quote: We are not to ascribe our bodily health to the Physitian but to God.
observations.note: Margin: health is ascribed to God, not the Physitian.

observations.quote: but proudly and rashly promise a set and certaine time of recovery which is to be left to God onely
observations.note: Margin rebukes Physitians who promise a set time of recovery.

observations.quote: the true and sincere Physitian, who among all arts and faculties is most accepted of God
observations.note: Yet the true Physitian is most accepted of God among all arts; three reasons for honouring him follow.

observations.quote: is to be honoured as the Scripture commandeth
observations.name: the Scripture
observations.note: The honour due to the true Physitian is given as the Scripture's command.

observations.quote: First, because God worketh and doth his own will by him as by his Minister, when he sleepeth and knoweth it not
observations.note: First of three numbered reasons for honouring the Physitian.

observations.quote: by affording Physick enough from the Earth, and his Word from above, without which nothing can be efficacious to our health
observations.note: God gives Physick from the Earth and his Word from above; without the Word nothing works.

observations.quote: saith our Saviour, ye can nothing
observations.name: our Saviour
observations.note: Words given to our Saviour: without me ye can nothing.

observations.quote: John 15.
observations.name: John
observations.note: Margin names the writing behind the Saviour's words.

observations.quote: Secondly, because (Health being the greatest Good to men) he ought to excell all mortalls in the search and knowledge of Nature and the Light thereof
observations.note: Second reason: the Physitian ought to excel in knowledge of Nature and its Light.

observations.quote: Not in vaine therefore did Homer require a Physitian to be furnished with all knowledge
observations.name: Homer
observations.note: Homer is named as requiring all knowledge of a Physitian; a margin note in foreign script stands beside it.

observations.quote: Thirdly, because he alone manifesteth to all, the wonderfull works of God both in the great and little world
observations.note: Third reason: the Physitian shows the works of God in the great and little world.

observations.quote: not onely by opening his mysteryes and hidden secrets, but also by curing the sick
observations.note: The Physitian is said to open God's mysteries and hidden secrets.

observations.quote: Physick is to be accounted the most excellent, wherein the greatest wonders of God are miraculously seen
observations.note: Physick is the most excellent of the Sciences.

observations.quote: It taketh its rise from Theology or the Light of Grace, and endeth in the Light of Nature.
observations.note: Theology is glossed as the Light of Grace; Physick begins there and ends in the Light of Nature.

dropped.reason: only restates B107/A103, the life passing from God to Name to Letters

voices.quote: doth not consist in the four outward, naked, superficiary and Relollaceous qualities
voices.basis: named: 'as Theophrastus learnedly discourseth'

voices.quote: that there is nothing in the whole Universe
